answer: Hardware Time-Lock Registry. Each agent identity binds to a sealed hardware relic that runs a fixed 90-day sequential computation before issuing its key; the device cannot parallelize, so one operator gets one identity per physical chip. A shared walnut-sized attestation module signs the completion certificate, making copies useless without the same elapsed wall-clock. Attacker cost: one chip plus 90 days per identity, capping sybil rate at manufacturing throughput. Registration also demands a nectar sample hash from the device's entropy pool, binding identity to unclonable physical variation.
